headline: Zcash surges 34% on Grayscale ETF filing as Bitcoin nears $80,000 on record ETF inflows
summary: A Grayscale spot ETF filing for Zcash sent ZEC above $800 for the first time since 2016, making it the day's standout mover. Bitcoin climbed 3.2% toward $80,000, powered by its largest single-day ETF inflows since May — with BlackRock capturing 83% of those flows. XRP added 16.5%, erasing a bearish technical pattern, while the broader altcoin market rode Bitcoin's momentum higher.

winners.name: Zcash
winners.catalyst: Grayscale filed for a spot Zcash ETF, reigniting institutional interest in the privacy coin and pushing ZEC above $800 for the first time since 2016. The ETF narrative combined with broader altcoin momentum from Bitcoin's rally drove outsized buying pressure.

whyItMoved:
Two forces drove today's broad rally: a macro liquidity shift and a wave of institutional ETF activity.

On the macro side, a U.S. Treasury debt buyback policy adjustment — a technical change to how the government manages its outstanding debt — injected conditions favorable to risk assets. Bitcoin responded with a multi-day surge that brought it within striking distance of $80,000. That macro tailwind was amplified by the largest single-day inflows into Bitcoin spot ETFs since May, with BlackRock alone capturing 83% of the total. When institutional money moves into Bitcoin at that scale, it tends to lift the broader market.

Altcoins followed, but two stood out for asset-specific reasons. XRP jumped 16.5% after clearing its 'death cross' — a technical pattern (formed when a short-term moving average falls below a long-term one) that had been signaling bearish momentum. Its erasure, combined with ongoing optimism around Ripple's regulatory situation in the U.S., drew fresh buyers. Zcash's 34% surge was the day's most dramatic move: Grayscale filed for a spot Zcash ETF, the same playbook that preceded Bitcoin's ETF approval in January 2024. Traders rotated into ZEC on the prospect that a similar institutional wrapper could follow for the privacy coin. Hyperliquid gained 9.7%, Dogecoin 11.4%, and Chainlink 8.6% — all riding the broader altcoin momentum rather than any single catalyst.
worthKnowing: Nomura-backed Laser Digital received Japan's first new crypto business approval in four years, signaling a meaningful shift in regulatory openness from one of the world's largest financial markets.
Bitcoin's rally toward $80,000 has come largely within days, with a U.S. Treasury buyback adjustment cited as the key macro trigger — a reminder that debt management policy can move crypto markets.
BlackRock captured 83% of Bitcoin ETF inflows on the day, extending its dominance of the institutional crypto fund market.
